clue.text: Criminal I becalm once still?

definitions.note: an old-fashioned apparatus for distilling; once marks it as historical

indicators.note: criminal as in shockingly wrong, so the letters of I becalm are set in a wrong order

explanation.surface: A villain asks whether he could ever calm down again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' looks like an adverb meaning yet, but it is the noun: distilling apparatus, and 'once' says the device is from the past.
explanation.definitionFit: An alembic is an antique distilling vessel used by alchemists, a still of former times.

clue.text: Walkers shunning top sportsmen

indicators.note: shunning top means avoiding the first letter, the top one in a down answer

parts.note: marchers are people who walk in a procession

explanation.surface: Athletes avoid the hillwalkers on the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' looks like a hilltop but means the first letter, M.
explanation.definitionFit: Archers are competitors in archery, a sport of shooting arrows at targets.

clue.text: German artist in France is holding service

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the French word goes around the other letters

parts.note: est is French for is
RN is the Royal Navy, one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A German painter in France takes part in a religious service.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German-born Dada and Surrealist painter and sculptor.

clue.text: Highwayman's gang nabbing equipment

indicators.note: nabbing means grabbing, so the group word takes the other letters inside

parts.note: a band is a gang
a rig is a piece of equipment or apparatus

explanation.surface: A highwayman's gang steals gear.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Highwayman stands for is, linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigand is a bandit who robs travellers on the road, just like a highwayman.

clue.text: Is able to rank urges, "A" being "something sweet"

parts.note: can means is able

indicators.note: to rank is to set in order, so urges and A are rearranged

parts.note: fodder for the anagram

explanation.surface: A teacher grades someone's impulses, giving an A meaning excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' reads as grading but rearranges URGES with A into ESUGAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Cane sugar is sucrose taken from sugar cane, a sweet substance.

clue.text: As Bottom, thespian at last in command

definitions.note: As is the chemical symbol of the element

parts.note: bottom means backside, crudely arse

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word thespian

parts.note: its last letter is used
IC is the abbreviation for in charge or in command

explanation.surface: A reference to Bottom, the Shakespeare character who is an actor, finally taking charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' at the front looks like a link word, but it is the chemical symbol and the definition. Bottom is the weaver-actor in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: As is the symbol on the periodic table for the poisonous element arsenic.

clue.text: Starting late, increasingly frantic summer?

definitions.note: one who sums, totting up figures

indicators.note: starting late means the word begins after its usual first letter

parts.note: madder means more crazed, increasingly frantic

explanation.surface: Summer starts late and grows ever more hectic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summer' looks like the season but is someone who sums; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: An adder is one who adds numbers together, which is what a summer does.

clue.text: Small-time writer denied opening design template

indicators.note: denied opening means the first letter is taken away

parts.note: a pencil is a writing implement

explanation.surface: A minor author is refused a first break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small-time' reads as minor but gives S and T separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A stencil is a cut-out sheet used to reproduce a pattern, a template for designs.

clue.text: Running with foremost in group in tight form of clothing

indicators.note: the second in places the jumbled letters inside the word for tight

parts.note: near can mean close or tight

indicators.note: running means the letters flow into a new arrangement

parts.note: fodder for the anagram

indicators.note: foremost in picks the leading letter of group

parts.note: its first letter is used

explanation.surface: Someone goes jogging with the leader of their club in tight sportswear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' looks like a description of the clothing, but it is the container, in its sense of close; the surface's 'in group' runner is only scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightwear is clothing such as pyjamas worn in bed, a type of garment.

clue.text: Cuirass ultimately included in my permitted body armour

indicators.note: included in means the letter goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: cor is an exclamation like my!
let means allowed or permitted

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter

parts.note: its last letter is used

explanation.surface: A cuirass is finally part of my approved protective kit.
explanation.walkthrough: Cuirass looks like the definition, but only its last letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A corslet is a piece of armour covering the torso, protecting the body.

clue.text: Transferred prisoner and authorised paperwork?

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner
to have signed paperwork is to have authorised it

explanation.surface: A prisoner is moved to another jail and the forms are approved.
explanation.definitionFit: To consign goods or people is to hand them over or send them on, so consigned means passed to another's keeping.

clue.text: Maybe Wallace and Gromit's initiator read Wrong Trousers

indicators.note: trousers as a verb means pockets or takes in, so one piece goes inside the other
wrong means the word read is put in the wrong order

parts.note: fodder for the anagram

indicators.note: the initiator is the starting letter of Gromit's

parts.note: its first letter is used

explanation.surface: Mentions the animated film The Wrong Trousers starring Wallace and Gromit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wallace' wants to be the cheese-loving inventor; it is Edgar Wallace, the thriller writer. 'Wrong' makes EDAR from READ and 'Trousers' puts G inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Wallace was a prolific British crime novelist; Maybe signals the first name is just one example.

clue.text: Catches parents bickering

indicators.note: bickering suggests quarrelling and disorder, so the letters of parents are jumbled

explanation.surface: A child overhears mother and father arguing.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap someone is to snare or trap them, the same as catching them out.

clue.text: Account about clubs and sex is genuine

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for genuine goes around the other letters

parts.note: genuine means real
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
it is a dated slang word for sex

explanation.surface: A story about nightclubs and sex is claimed to be true.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a detailed telling or narration of events, an account of them.

clue.text: Suddenly hurls back stringed instrument

indicators.note: back means the verb meaning suddenly hurls is read from end to start

parts.note: darts as a verb means moves or throws suddenly

explanation.surface: Someone flings a violin backwards in a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: A Strad is short for a Stradivarius, a violin or cello made by the famous Cremona luthier.

clue.text: We mitigate excess, missing nothing in banks

definitions.note: we, a plural subject, who ease or lessen things

indicators.note: in places the shortened word inside the word for banks

parts.note: to bank on something is to rely on it, so banks means relies

indicators.note: missing means the letter for nothing is taken out

parts.note: over means excess, as in surplus
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone in finance says they rein in waste without leaving any gap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' looks like money institutions but is the verb meaning relies; OVER loses its O to give VER.
explanation.definitionFit: Relievers are people or things that ease pain or distress, so they lessen it.

clue.text: Most difficult integrals cracked

indicators.note: cracked means broken apart, so the letters of integrals are rearranged

explanation.surface: A student finally solves the hardest calculus problems.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnarly is slang for tricky or awkward, so the superlative is the hardest of all.

clue.text: Most ingenious radio broadcast on cricket match

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first part sits above the second
broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of radio are rearranged

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: The cleverest radio coverage of a cricket game.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is a top-level international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means skilful and clever, so the superlative describes the most skilful.

clue.text: Rescuer, one who resides in Bucks?

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the plural for male animals

parts.note: bucks are male deer, so the plural noun deer
a liver is someone who lives, that is resides, somewhere

explanation.surface: Asks whether a saviour is someone living in Buckinghamshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Bucks looks like the English county Buckinghamshire, but it is male deer.
explanation.definitionFit: A deliverer is one who sets others free, a saviour or rescuer.

clue.text: Hopelessness shown by some French couple

parts.note: des is French for some
a pair is a couple

explanation.surface: A French couple are in despair.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is complete loss of hope, so it equals hopelessness.

clue.text: US Vice President accepts large European bond

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so the name surrounds the other letters

parts.note: JD Vance is a US Vice President

explanation.surface: A US Vice President agrees to a big European financial bond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bond' reads as a financial instrument but is the chemical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry, valence is an atom's capacity to combine, measured by the bonds it forms.

clue.text: County idiots

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the abbreviation for Berkshire, an English county west of London
second meaning: British slang for fools

explanation.walkthrough: Berks is short for Berkshire, a county west of London; a berk is a British word for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the shortened county name and the plural of a mild British insult for stupid people.

clue.text: One Kenneth Grahame, not the writer, vacuous Bohemian eccentric

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, so the letters are put in a strange order
not means the following piece is left out

parts.note: the surname of the author of The Wind in the Willows
the writer refers to the setter, i.e. me

indicators.note: vacuous means emptied, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: its first and last letters are used

explanation.surface: Kenneth Grahame, author of The Wind in the Willows, is called an odd bohemian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kenneth Grahame' looks like one name, but Kenneth goes with the definition. GRAHA plus BN is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Kenneth Branagh is the actor-director, so he is one person called Kenneth.

clue.text: Could they briefly hide tackle in water polo?

definitions.text: Could they briefly hide tackle in water polo?

parts.words: Could they briefly hide tackle in water polo?
parts.note: brand-name swimming briefs; briefly hints at briefs, and tackle is slang for male genitals

explanation.walkthrough: 'tackle' reads as a sporting challenge but is slang for male genitals, and 'briefly' hints at briefs.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedos are close-fitting swimming trunks, a brand of brief worn by swimmers and polo players.

clue.text: Henry introduced to vendor who collects 24s?

parts.note: a vendor is a seller
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.walkthrough: Henry looks like a man's name, but it is the physics unit whose symbol is H.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheller is someone who gathers shellfish or removes shells, as an abalone collector would.

clue.text: Settle old scores, finally stopping nonsense

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so the letters go inside the word for nonsense

parts.note: rot means nonsense

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter

parts.note: its last letter is used

explanation.surface: Someone resolves old disputes, at last putting an end to foolishness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settle old scores' reads as revenge, but only 'Settle' is the definition, in the sense of birds alighting.
explanation.definitionFit: To roost is to perch or settle down for rest, as birds do.

clue.text: Man trouble is concerning clothes

indicators.note: clothes as a verb means dresses or covers, so the outer letters wrap around the word for trouble

parts.note: re means concerning, about
ado means fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A man's problem has to do with his wardrobe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' reads as a noun about garments but works as a verb meaning wraps.
explanation.definitionFit: Isadore is a male first name, so it is one example of a man.

clue.text: Abalone, first of two with no top

indicators.note: with no top means the first letter, the top in a down answer, is removed

parts.note: the former is the first of two things mentioned

explanation.surface: A shellfish dish is described as the first of two, served without its shell.
explanation.definitionFit: An ormer is the Channel Islands name for the abalone, an edible sea snail.

clue.text: Some private income put away in one's home?

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A wealthy person stashes unearned income at home.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat in is to have a meal at home; put away is slang for eating food.

clue.text: Cordially receiving Oscar, writer introduces dream novel

parts.note: O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of dream are rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book the writer presents, but it signals that DREAM becomes ARMED.
explanation.definitionFit: To welcome someone with open arms is to greet them warmly, so the adjective describes a hearty reception.

clue.text: Consideration shown by others outside church, quietly reflecting

indicators.note: outside means the word for others goes around the remaining letters

parts.note: the rest means the others

p is the musical marking piano, quietly

explanation.walkthrough: 'reflecting' looks like quiet thought outside church but turns CEP round to make PEC.
explanation.definitionFit: Respect is regard or esteem, giving due consideration to someone.

clue.text: Tops shortlist revised after 3rd- and 6th- placed drop out

definitions.note: tops are upper garments, a plural noun

indicators.note: revised means changed, so the remaining letters are put in a new order
the letters in the third and sixth places of shortlist are removed

explanation.surface: The leaders of a shortlist change after two candidates withdraw.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the 3rd and 6th letters, O and L, leaves SHRTIST, which 'revised' rearranges. 'Tops' looks like a verb or the leaders but means garments.
explanation.definitionFit: T-shirts are casual short-sleeved upper garments, a kind of top.
